raw_response:
I have been farming these 16.9 mu in Quzhou for forty years, and I know what works here. The wheat-maize double cropping is the backbone of my farm—it feeds the family and provides steady income. This year I will keep about 13 mu in that rotation and plant 3.9 mu to cotton, which brings cash but needs too much hand-picking labor for me to expand now that some of my family works off-farm. For the wheat, I will sow an improved variety like Jimai 22 in early October, rotary till the land, apply around 18 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu, irrigate three times from my well, and spray four times for weeds and diseases; I expect about 500 kg per mu. Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize—probably Denghai 605—with no-tillage to save time, give it 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu, irrigate twice, spray three times, and expect about 550 kg per mu. For the cotton, I will rotary till the 3.9 mu in spring, sow an improved Bt variety, apply 9 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu, irrigate twice, and spray about sixteen times because bollworms and aphids are relentless; I hope for around 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.
